title: The way in from outside
description: GET /v1/tunnel, this machine's own token only (a paired device is 403): what the cloudflared this daemon runs is doing. It is turned on and off by `remote_tunnel` in the settings (POST /v1/settings), and it refuses to start while nothing but this machine is let in. A quick tunnel's address is its secret, which is why a paired phone cannot read this.

attempts.description: Launches in a row that have died, while it is retrying; absent when none have.

binary.description: The cloudflared the next launch would run: `cloudflared_path` when it is set and executable, else where a package manager puts it, else PATH. Absent when there is none.

changed.description: When state, url or reason last moved.

command.description: The command line of the child that is running or was last started, binary first. It always carries `--config` and this daemon's own file, never the person's ~/.cloudflared/config.yml.

config.description: The configuration file cloudflared is pointed at, in this daemon's state directory.

reason.description: Why it failed or refused, in the tunnel's own sentence. Present when state is failed.

url.description: The address, once a connection to Cloudflare's edge is registered. Present when state is up.

TunnelMode.description: `off`; `quick`, an address made up per run under trycloudflare.com; `named`, the person's own tunnel (`remote_tunnel_name`) and hostname (`remote_hostname`).

TunnelState.description: `off`; `starting`, launched or waiting to retry and not yet registered with the edge; `up`; `failed`, with a reason — including a refusal to start.
